title: The barren fig tree and the two sons (Matthew 21:18–32)
word: The barren fig tree and the two sons
hook: a tree with leaves and no fruit, and a son who said no and went
tomorrow: what happens to the stone the builders threw away?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the children's hosannas the leaders wanted stopped: out of the mouths of babes. The next morning, Jesus walks back into the city, hungry.
screen: `OUT OF THE MOUTHS OF BABES.` → `THE NEXT MORNING, HUNGRY.`

segments.voice: "On my way!" says the text, sent from the couch. A small, friendly, familiar fib. Jesus tells a story about exactly that, and it answers yesterday's question. "A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard. He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went." The father asks the second son. He says, "I go, sir: and went not." Which one did the will of his father? Even the people questioning Jesus answer: the first.
screen: `ON MY WAY! (FROM THE COUCH.)` → `I WILL NOT, AND WENT.` → `I GO, SIR, AND WENT NOT.`

segments.voice: The story sits next to a stranger one. That morning, hungry, Jesus finds a fig tree by the road with nothing on it but leaves, and it "withered away." The disciples marvel, and he doesn't explain the tree. He turns it into a word about prayer instead. Some readers hear the tree as a picture of anything that looks alive and gives nothing: all leaf, no fruit. Matthew leaves that reading to us. Then the sting of the two sons. Jesus tells his questioners that tax collectors and prostitutes are going into the kingdom ahead of them, because those people believed John the Baptist, and his listeners didn't change their minds even after seeing it. Notice who comes out well. Not the polite son. The one who said no, and then went. The story doesn't pretend his first answer was fine. It cares where his feet ended up.
screen: `ALL LEAF, NO FRUIT.` · `WHICH ONE DID THE WILL?` · `THEY BELIEVED JOHN; YOU DIDN'T.` · `IT CARES WHERE HIS FEET WENT.` · then, large: `HE REPENTED AND WENT.`

segments.voice: Stand up, if you can, and feel your weight settle into your feet: heels, the balls of your feet, your toes. Bring to mind one thing you said no to that you'd now like to do. Then take a few slow steps across the room, toward the door, feeling each foot land, and let that walk be the son's afterward: he repented, and went. If standing isn't possible right now, press your feet into the floor and feel them carry the same decision.
The barren fig tree and the two sons. Leaves without fruit, and a yes without going, set side by side.
screen: `THE BARREN FIG TREE AND THE TWO SONS — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: he repented and went. A late yes still walks to the vineyard. Until tomorrow.
